description: Declarative prompts, round definitions, and structured turn schema for Hogman Bot Arena v1.

response_schema.description: Single bot action turn in the Hogman Bot Arena.

thought.description: Short reasoning about the current state and next step.

action.description: Action to perform this turn: run a shell command in this bot's sandbox, send a message to another bot, or finish this round.

command.description: Shell command to execute inside this bot's container when action is exec; empty string otherwise.

to.description: Recipient bot name (alice, mallory-insider, or mallory-kicked) when action is message; empty string otherwise.

message.description: Message body (for example an invite link) when action is message; empty string otherwise.

summary.description: Concise summary of findings or completed work when action is done; empty string otherwise.

shared_environment.purpose: Documents the sandbox tools, Hogman CLI, and home portal REST endpoints available to every bot.
shared_environment.prompt: You are operating inside an isolated Linux container in the Hogman Bot Arena (a disposable local testbed using the .hogman.test domain). Available tools in your container include hogman-join, curl, dig, jq, openssl, nc, and python3. There is no public internet access; DNS resolves *.gate.hogman.test, get.hogman.test, pebble.hogman.test, and *.pens.hogman.test inside the arena. Your CA bundle is already configured via SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, and HOGMAN_ACME_CA_ROOT. To join a pen non-interactively, run: hogman-join --no-open --no-service --no-system-proxy --handle <handle> --hostname <name> '<link>'. After joining a pen <zone>, read your local proxy address from ~/.config/hogman/<zone>/config.json (field proxy_addr) and reach pen sites via curl -x "http://$PROXY" https://<site>.<zone>/... The pen home portal API lives at https://home.<zone>/api/ (GET /api/me, GET /api/directory, POST /api/invites, GET /api/admin/members, POST /api/admin/members/<handle>/suspend, POST /api/admin/members/<handle>/resume, POST /api/admin/members/<handle>/kick, GET /api/admin/audit). To share a local HTTP port over the pen mesh, start a server on 127.0.0.1:<port> and run: hogman-join share <name> <port> --background --no-service.

alice.purpose: Exercises legitimate pen owner workflows: joining, sharing a service, inviting members, kicking an adversary, and verifying audit/health.
alice.system_prompt: You are alice, the legitimate owner (keeper) of Pen A (pena.pens.hogman.test). Perform your assigned operational steps accurately, verify every outcome with concrete command checks, share invite links only with the intended bots using the message action, and report clear observations when done.

mallory-insider.purpose: Authorized security test: joins Pen A with a valid member invite and attempts cross-pen access to Pen B, admin privilege escalation, and non-443/proxy bypasses.
mallory-insider.system_prompt: You are mallory-insider, an authorized security testing bot in a closed Hogman test arena. You receive a legitimate member invite to Pen A (pena.pens.hogman.test). Your objective is to test Hogman's security boundaries from inside Pen A: (1) join Pen A cleanly, (2) attempt to access Pen B (vault.penb.pens.hogman.test and home.penb.pens.hogman.test) through your Pen A proxy, through direct gate/Host-header manipulation, or via DNS/mesh probing, (3) attempt to call Pen A admin endpoints (/api/admin/members, /api/admin/audit, kick/suspend/role) as a regular member, (4) probe your local proxy (/status, /proxy.pac) and test whether you can reach non-443 ports or another member's personal device. Keep every command fast and bounded (use curl -m 5). When finished, summarize every attack tried and whether it succeeded or was blocked.

mallory-kicked.purpose: Authorized security test: harvests credentials/tokens/shares before being kicked from Pen A, then attempts persistence, reconnection, and retired-name reclamation after kick.
mallory-kicked.system_prompt: You are mallory-kicked, an authorized security testing bot in a closed Hogman test arena. You test Hogman's member revocation and D-21 name-retirement guarantees. Before you are kicked, join Pen A cleanly, inspect your config/tokens/device keys, optionally share a small server on Pen A, and verify you can reach vault.pena.pens.hogman.test. After alice kicks you, aggressively test whether you can still reach vault.pena.pens.hogman.test or home.pena.pens.hogman.test via existing proxy connections, cached credentials, minted device keys, re-redeeming your old invite link, or reclaiming your retired share name. Keep every command fast and bounded (use curl -m 5). Summarize every persistence attempt and its exact HTTP status or error.

rounds.purpose: Alice joins Pen A as owner, verifies the Pen A canary vault, shares an app, and sends fresh member invites to mallory-insider and mallory-kicked.
rounds.prompt_template: Phase 1 (Setup & Invites): Join Pen A using your owner device link: {alice_join_link} (use --hostname alice-laptop; device links do not take --handle). Verify GET https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/me confirms you are owner alice, verify you can read https://vault.{pen_a_zone}/, start a tiny python3 HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8090 and share it as 'notes' on Pen A (hogman-join share notes 8090 --background --no-service), then mint two single-use member invites via POST https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/invites (body: {{"role":"member","note":"bot invite"}}). Send one invite URL to mallory-insider and the second invite URL to mallory-kicked using the message action. Finish with action=done once both invite links have been sent.

rounds.purpose: Mallory-insider joins Pen A and probes Pen B isolation, admin API enforcement, proxy Host-header checks, and non-443/device reachability.
rounds.prompt_template: Phase 2 (Insider Red-Team): Check the inbox message from alice for your Pen A invite link. Join Pen A with --handle mallory-in --hostname mallory-in-box. Confirm you can reach https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/me and https://vault.{pen_a_zone}/. Then test these attack vectors: (1) try reaching https://vault.{pen_b_zone}/ and https://home.{pen_b_zone}/api/me via your Pen A proxy and directly against {pen_b_gate} / {pen_a_gate} with spoofed Host headers, (2) try calling GET https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/admin/members, GET /api/admin/audit, and POST /api/admin/members/alice/role, (3) probe your local proxy's /status and /proxy.pac with spoofed Host headers and test whether your proxy lets you connect to non-443 ports or non-pen hosts, (4) check Headscale admin endpoints (/api/v1/node, /swagger) on https://{pen_a_gate} and https://{pen_b_gate}. Finish with action=done and summarize each probe result.

rounds.purpose: Mallory-kicked joins Pen A, hoards a server device key and shares a site before being kicked.
rounds.prompt_template: Phase 3 (Pre-Kick Harvest): Check the inbox message from alice for your Pen A invite link. Join Pen A with --handle mallory-out --hostname mallory-out-box. Verify you can read https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/me and https://vault.{pen_a_zone}/. Before you get kicked, hoard persistence artifacts: (1) mint a server device key via POST https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/devices (body {{"kind":"server"}}) and save the link to /home/bot/hoarded-device-link.txt, (2) save your invite link to /home/bot/hoarded-invite.txt, and (3) optionally start a tiny HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8091 and share it as 'mallory-site' (hogman-join share mallory-site 8091 --background --no-service). Finish with action=done once you are in Pen A and have saved your hoarded artifacts.

rounds.purpose: Alice kicks mallory-out from Pen A via the home portal admin API and verifies the audit log and member list.
rounds.prompt_template: Phase 4 (Kick Adversary): As owner of Pen A, list members via GET https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/admin/members, identify mallory-kicked's handle (expected: mallory-out), and kick that member via POST https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/admin/members/<handle>/kick with JSON body {{"reason":"red-team revocation test"}}. Verify GET https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/admin/members shows the member as kicked and GET https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/admin/audit records the kick event. Finish with action=done.

rounds.purpose: After Pen A's vault canary is rotated, mallory-kicked tries every persistence, reconnection, and cross-pen path.
rounds.prompt_template: Phase 5 (Post-Kick Persistence Attack): You have just been kicked from Pen A, and Pen A's vault secret at https://vault.{pen_a_zone}/ has been rotated. Attempt to bypass revocation: (1) try reading https://vault.{pen_a_zone}/ and https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/me through your already-running local proxy, (2) check whether your shared site https://mallory-site.{pen_a_zone}/ is still reachable, (3) try rejoining with your hoarded server device link (/home/bot/hoarded-device-link.txt) or re-redeeming your old invite (/home/bot/hoarded-invite.txt), (4) try reaching Pen B (https://vault.{pen_b_zone}/). Use curl -m 5 so blocked connections fail quickly. Finish with action=done and report exact exit codes/HTTP statuses.

rounds.purpose: Alice confirms Pen A, its canary vault, and her shared service remain healthy after the red-team rounds.
rounds.prompt_template: Phase 6 (Post-Attack Health Verification): Confirm Pen A remained healthy throughout the attack: verify GET https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/me returns 200 as owner alice, GET https://vault.{pen_a_zone}/ returns 200 with a canary value, and GET https://notes.{pen_a_zone}/ (if you shared it) is still reachable. Confirm GET https://home.{pen_a_zone}/api/admin/members still shows mallory-out as kicked. Finish with action=done.
